function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

It sounds like you’re looking for a virtual companion—an AI “girlfriend.” I can help you think through what that might look like and suggest some ways to get started. Here are a few options: | Option | What it involves | Pros | Cons | |--------|------------------|------|------| | **Use an existing chatbot platform** (e.g., Replika, Mitsuku, or a custom GPT‑based bot) | You can chat with a pre‑trained model that’s already designed for companionship. | • Easy to set up
• Already has personality settings | • Limited customization
• May not feel “real” enough | | **Build your own chatbot** using GPT‑4 or similar | Write prompts, set personality traits, and fine‑tune responses. | • Full control over tone, interests, and behavior
• Can integrate with other services (calendar, music, etc.) | • Requires some coding
• Needs ongoing maintenance | | **Create a “virtual girlfriend” app** | Combine a chatbot with a UI, avatar, and interactive features (games, reminders, etc.). | • Immersive experience
• Can add multimedia elements | • More complex development
• Might need graphics/design skills | ### How to get started 1. **Define the personality** - Think about traits you’d like (e.g., supportive, humorous, curious). - Decide on interests (music, movies, hobbies). 2. **Choose a platform** - For quick prototyping, try Replika or a GPT‑4 playground. - For deeper customization, use the OpenAI API. 3. **Set up conversation flows** - Draft common scenarios (greeting, daily check‑in, conflict resolution). - Use prompt engineering to guide responses. 4. **Add extra features** - Calendar integration for reminders. - Music or video playback. - Voice synthesis for a more natural feel. 5. **Test and iterate** - Have friends or yourself chat with it. - Refine prompts based on feedback. If you’d like, I can help you draft a personality profile or write sample prompts for a GPT‑4 chatbot. Just let me know what aspects matter most to you!
